text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- A Constitutional Tribunal decision this week allowing for equal treatment of state-owned and private liquid fuels' importers will enhance competition in the sector, the Polish Liquid Fuels' Chamber (PIPP) president Andrzej Szczesniak said.
- Nafta Polska will issue one-year commercial papers worth up to 30 million zlotys, Warsaw-based Bank Handlowy said.
- The Era GSM digital mobile phone network will cover 30 Polish cities by the end of this year.
- Finance Minister Grzegorz Kolodko hopes that he will convince the senate to amend the recently passed taxation bill.

- Elblag province authorities want the city to become an international Baltic port and are negotiating the right of third-party ships' passage through the Russian-controlled Pilawa strait. Russia now allows free passage only to Polish ships.
- Polish market gardeners have suffered from falling market prices and excessive harvesting costs caused by exceptionally good harvests this year.
- Russia's central bank has invited Poland's Bank Handlowy (BH) to open a subsidiary in Russia, BH representatives said. BH is likely to start the new operation by the 1997-end.
- Listed construction firm Elektrobudowa will supply the Kujawy SA cement mill with mobile container stations worth 295,000 zlotys.
NOWA EUROPA
- The EkoFund Foundation will provide 10 million zlotys in subsidies to nine environmental projects around Poland, EkoFund's president Maciej Nowicki said.
- France's Leclerc will build a trade and service centre in Lublin, eastern Poland, to start operating in 1998.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- Poles will consume more low-fat milk, cheese, yoghurts and icecreams and less butter and sour cream in future years, Agricultural Economy Institute professor Aldon Zalewski said.
- International investment funds have invested $8 million in shares of the Polish Starfood potato chips maker.
- The Lodz-based Cin Cin distillery holding will present a share issue prospectus to the Polish Securities Commission (KPW) in the next few weeks. Bank Gdanski brokerage house will manage the issue.
ZYCIE
- More than 40 percent of Poles think that Poland's economic situation is bad and only 16 percent think otherwise, a survey by the CBOS opinion poll said.
- Poligrafia SA printing firm, controlled by the listed Exbud capital group, will issue 1,375,280 F-series shares at 2.5 zlotys which will inject capital to its modernisation fund.
- Only 32,000 new flats were built in Poland this year to the end of September, which was the worst result in many years, the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said.
PARKIET

- A tax to be introduced next year on off-bourse sales of mass privatisation National Investment Fund (NFI) units will not affect the buyers' interests in these securities and will only limit the so-called grey-sphere, market analysts said.
- The Warsaw bourse board will enter Polisa, Lubawa and Kompap shares as well as the new share issues by Tonsil and Exbud for continuous trading on the main market in mid- November.

- Obudsman Adam Zielinski has approached the prime minister to extend the distribution period of the NFI privatisation certificates so that 200,000 homeless Poles can collect them. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
